title: Sundown soft-launch — tactile checkpad & region ripple plan (Nov 2026)
content:
Objective:
A light-weight, tactile checklist and 48-hour regional ripple plan for a controlled soft-launch during low-traffic hours (sundown window). This document is intentionally terse — designed for on-call operators and launch shepherds to read quickly and act.

Context / scope:
- Target: small feature flip that modifies model routing for a subset of traffic (10% global -> progressive regional ramp).
- Window: 23:00–02:00 PT (local night across primary NA region), with staged handoffs to EU/APAC the following nights if green.
- Goal: validate routing, latency tails, and cost delta while preserving safety and fast rollbacks.

Quick rules (one-line):
- Always keep a warm fallback variant pinned and health-checked. If any of the top 3 latency or error gates breach, immediate rollback to fallback.
- One engineer per shard/region + one orchestration lead. No more than 3 active changes simultaneously.

Staffing & contact ladder:
- Orchestration lead: Rohit Menon (pager + slack)
- NA shift: Maya (primary), Luca (secondary)
- EU watch: Zoe (on-call read-only until green)
- APAC follow: Priya (standby for day-2 expansion)
- Incident comms: #release-nightwatch -> escalate to #eng-oncall -> exec-alert if SLA breach > 15m

Pre-launch checks (T-72h to T-1h):
- T-72h: Confirm canary config in feature flags and that config repo PR merged (linked artifact).
- T-48h: Run synthetic traffic generator against canary routing for 6 hours (latency distribution snapshot). Attach graphs to Jira RL-4021.
- T-24h: Freeze non-essential infra changes; confirm telemetry retention window and sampling (see telemetry knobs below).
- T-4h: Verify runbook references and ensure fallback images pinned in Dedicated pools.
- T-1h: Signal go/no-go on Slack, confirm staffing, set burn-in endpoint to 1% traffic for 15 minutes.

Telemetry sampling and smoke gates (what we watch + thresholds):
- Metrics to sample at 10s granularity (during first 60m), 60s after stable:
  - p50/p95/p99 latency (in ms) for model-route and total request path
  - error rate (5xx + model decode failures)
  - tail CPU/GPU utilization and queue length on serving nodes
  - request abandon/drop and connection resets
  - cost-per-token estimate (quick micro-billing sample)
- Gates (immediate rollback triggers):
  - p99 latency increases > 40% vs baseline for 5 consecutive minutes
  - error rate > 0.5% sustained for 3 minutes
  - GPU OOM or node-level instability (any crash loop)
  - Telemetry ingestion drop > 10% (loss of visibility)

Regional ripple schedule (staged, conservative):
- Night 0 (NA): 1% -> 5% after 15m -> 10% after 45m -> hold 60m -> evaluate
- Night 1 (EU): mirror NA progression but start at 0.5% -> 3% -> 7% with 90m hold at 7%
- Night 2 (APAC): start 0.5% and only progress if both NA & EU fully green for 24h
- Each step requires explicit green-check (telemetry snapshot + human confirmation) from region lead

Smoke test matrix (quick checks to run at each ramp step):
- Functional: sample 10 representative requests across routes — verify responses are within acceptance heuristics (no hallucination drift; structured tool outputs intact).
- Latency: run 50 synthetic threads to hit 95th percentile — ensure p95 within gate
- Cost sanity: compare token cost sample to expected +/-10%
- Secondary checks: tracing spans present, KV cache hits consistent, prefix cache hit rate unchanged

Rollback & mitigation ladder (fast actions):
- Soft rollback (0–5m): reduce traffic back to previous step and keep canary live for 15m while diagnosing
- Full rollback (5–30m): flip feature flag to fallback, block rollout in other regions, open incident in Jira, notify execs if user-facing SLA affected
- Emergency evacuation (>30m or critical instability): remove canary from all pools and trigger auto-scale to baseline capacity; start postmortem slate

Post-launch notes & immediate follow-ups (T+0 to T+72h):
- T+0–4h: gather first-pass notes in this doc: deviations, anomalies, mitigation steps taken, graphs inserted (attach links).
- T+24h: consolidated telemetry export and readout; compare to pre-launch run.
- T+72h: decision on full expansion OR rollback based on sustained signal and QA acceptance.

Open questions & friction points (notes to self):
- Can we reduce telemetry sampling cost without losing visibility? Need follow-up with observability team (Zoe).
- Are dedicated pool fallback images synced across regions? Last sync check shows a 6-hour lag — need to confirm with infra.
- Who owns the cost-per-token micro-billing script used in the checks? (Linked PR above looks like it but needs owner).

Action items (owners):
- Maya: run synthetic generator T-48h (attach outputs to RL-4021) — due 2026-11-05
- Zoe: confirm telemetry retention & sampling knobs for night window — due 2026-11-06
- Luca: validate fallback image sync across Dedicated pools — due 2026-11-06
- Priya: prep EU nightwatch notes and high-latency contact list — due 2026-11-07

Quick shorthand (for launch shepherds):
- Green = p99 < +20% and errors < 0.2% and no node crashes.
- Yellow = escalation to orchestration lead, hold progression + 30m.
- Red = immediate rollback and incident open.

Notes to self / log:
- 2026-11-03 09:12 — initial draft created after sync with observability; flagged telemetry cost question.
- 2026-11-04 15:47 — updated rollback thresholds after infra suggestion (lowered error threshold).

End-of-doc: keep this file minimal and iterative. This is the field version for night ops; after a successful soft-launch we’ll convert to a formal runbook with screenshots and exact dashboard links.
